label: Huitzilopochtli is in Coatlicue's womb in this Book 3 account
continuity: Florentine Codex, Book 3 Coatepec narrative (colonial Nahuatl/Spanish witness)

supports: Huitzilopochtli is still in his mother Coatlicue's womb.

note: Restricted to the specified narrative witness.

label: Coyolxauhqui is named as Coatlicue's daughter
continuity: Florentine Codex, Book 3 Coatepec narrative (colonial Nahuatl/Spanish witness)

supports: Coyolxauhqui is with the Centzonhuitznahuah in their plan to kill their mother Coatlicue.

note: Restricted to the specified narrative witness.

label: Coyolxauhqui leads the attack that Huitzilopochtli defeats
continuity: Florentine Codex, Book 3 Coatepec narrative (colonial Nahuatl/Spanish witness)

supports: Huitzilopochtli has Coyolxauhqui struck by xiuhcoatl and defeats the attacking group.

note: The relation records an event in the cited account, not a universal moral alignment.

label: Cuahuitl Ihcac warns Huitzilopochtli of the approaching attack
continuity: Florentine Codex, Book 3 Coatepec narrative (colonial Nahuatl/Spanish witness)

supports: Cuahuitl Ihcac informs Huitzilopochtli about the attackers' deliberations and approach.

note: The Spanish witness calls him a traitor in relation to the attackers; this graph label records his direct assistance to Huitzilopochtli only.

label: Tochancalqui lights xiuhcoatl at Huitzilopochtli's direction
continuity: Florentine Codex, Book 3 Coatepec narrative (colonial Nahuatl/Spanish witness)

supports: Huitzilopochtli tells Tochancalqui to light xiuhcoatl, and Tochancalqui does so.

note: A specific narrative action, not a permanent faction affiliation.

label: Quetzalcoatl takes the precious bones despite Mictlantecuhtli's attempt to have them returned
continuity: Leyenda de los Soles, Códice Chimalpopoca (colonial Nahuatl witness via UNAM edition)

citations.locator: Leyenda de los Soles, UNAM ed., p. 120
supports: Mictlantecuhtli sends messengers to tell Quetzalcoatl to return the bones; Quetzalcoatl takes them away.

note: A relation in this one Leyenda sequence, not a total account of either figure.

label: Cihuacoatl prepares the bones at Tamoanchan before Quetzalcoatl's blood act
continuity: Leyenda de los Soles, Códice Chimalpopoca (colonial Nahuatl witness via UNAM edition)

note: The relation is sequential and source-specific; it does not establish a creator/created relation.

label: Nanahuatzin and Nahuitecpatl undertake the paired fire/ash sequence
continuity: Leyenda de los Soles, Códice Chimalpopoca (colonial Nahuatl witness via UNAM edition)

citations.locator: Leyenda de los Soles, UNAM ed., pp. 121–122
supports: Nanahuatl enters the fire while the Moon/Nahuitecpatl enters the ashes; both then reach the sky in the account.

note: A bounded sequence relation, not a claim that their identities or cosmological functions are universal.

label: Tlahuizcalpantecuhtli shoots at the Sun, which shoots back
continuity: Leyenda de los Soles, Códice Chimalpopoca (colonial Nahuatl witness via UNAM edition)

citations.locator: Leyenda de los Soles, UNAM ed., p. 122
supports: Tlahuizcalpantecuhtli shoots at the Sun; the Sun returns the shot and covers his face with the nine heavens.

note: The opposition is one narrative moment in the cited translation.
